rationale: Base config: trainer defaults tuned in the single-algorithm cards.
Lower learning rate: smaller steps on high-variance Monte-Carlo gradients.
Higher learning rate: tests whether the policy collapses early (low entropy).
Shorter horizon: lower-variance returns, less credit for long-term effects.
No baseline: plain REINFORCE, the variance-reduction reference.
Scalar moving-average baseline instead of a learned V(s).
Raw advantages: no per-batch scale normalisation.
Stronger entropy bonus: keeps exploring longer.
Fewer episodes per update: more, noisier updates.
More episodes per update: fewer, lower-variance updates.
